summary: The change adds exact hub-origin and session CSRF checks to the shared approve and deny handler, renders the requesting client, audience, label and requested lifetime on the consent page, and adds cross-origin approve and deny regressions that leave the attacker-held device code pending.

evidence: `src/passport.ts` now calls `ensureHubSessionCsrfToken` and `mutationHasHubOrigin` before any device approve or deny mutation.
`src/passport.ts` adds `clientId`, `audience`, `ttlDays` and `csrfToken` to the device bootstrap; `public/device-view.js` renders the consent details and `public/device.js` sends `x-csrf-token`.
`src/handler_test.ts` and `tests/bun_test.ts` add cross-origin approve and deny regressions that assert 403 responses and a still-pending attacker-held device code.
